_comment: One reviewed disposition for every GitHub workflow (#400). Until this inventory existed, `.github/workflows/` was governed only by the gates that happened to parse it: stream1-diagnostic.yml sat pinned to a branch deleted after #373 landed, swallowing every failure with `|| true`, unable to fail and reading to every agent as an active pattern. ACTIVE = event-triggered gate or automation; its trigger branches must be live remote refs (or reviewed retained_branches rows). MANUAL_DIAGNOSTIC = workflow_dispatch-only, an on-demand measurement an operator or agent invokes deliberately. RETIRED = removed; names `replaced_by` (what now covers its function), a `removal_owner` and a `removal_issue` -- a retirement is a decision, not permission to resurrect, so a RETIRED file that reappears on disk fails the gate. Checked by scripts/check-workflow-inventory.py in both directions (a workflow file with no entry fails; an entry naming no file fails), plus the three rots that let stream1 go unnoticed: dead trigger branches, pinned commits the repository no longer contains, and blanket error swallowing (`|| true`, `continue-on-error: true`) with no written reason within six lines. The gate does NOT verify that a workflow's declared job graph still does what its rationale says; rationales are reviewed prose, not proofs.

workflows.rationale: Guards the workflow cage on PRs and merge-queue candidates: the write-safety and required-checks declarations must hold on the tree being merged.

The primary test gate: unit suites, service-backed suites (Postgres/MinIO), hive-conductor e2e, wheel imports and the docker build, on PRs, merge-queue candidates and pushes to the maintained branches.
GitHub CodeQL static analysis over the Python code, on PRs, pushes to main and a weekly schedule.
Regenerates the compliance evidence bundle from quality/compliance-registry.json on pushes to the maintained branches; on-demand for evidence rebuilds.
Microsoft DevSkim SAST on PRs, pushes to develop and a weekly schedule.
Enqueues eligible PRs into the merge queue after a qualifying workflow_run, with a scheduled sweep and a manual entry point.
On-demand apisec ethicalcheck DAST probe against a deployed target; dispatch-only because it needs operator-supplied target input.
Nightly full Hypothesis property-conformance sweep on a schedule; dispatch for replaying a night on demand.
Property-based formal conformance on every PR, merge-queue candidate and push to the maintained branches.
Gateway smoke: installs through the documented path, proves the migration chain across the Postgres major upgrade, and tears down clean.
Execution-evidence publisher (#262 AC-2): after a CI/quality run, verifies every required check actually reported on the exact candidate head.
Aggregate check for specialized integration evidence: every classifier-selected specialized job (services, e2e, containers) must have completed on the candidate.
On-demand merge-queue latency measurement over a caller-supplied window; a diagnostic, not a gate.
Full cosmic-ray mutation run on demand; the PR-blocking mutation subset lives in quality.yml, so this is the deep-measurement diagnostic.
The 8-pillar PR-blocking bag: coverage, property tests, code smells, types, mutation subset, contracts, architecture fitness, docstrings -- plus the repository's inventory and ratchet gates.
Spec/ADR registry conformance: the ADR and SPEC corpus must stay machine-checkable against the registry CLI.
Publishes the release on v* tags: builds the pinned images, scans, signs and pushes with provenance.
Builds and attaches the platform installers on v* tags (push) with a dispatch entry point for rebuilds.
On-demand RSI harvest over operator-supplied inputs; runs the self-improvement loop in its container boundary by explicit request only.
On-demand runner cost census over a caller-supplied window; a measurement diagnostic, never blocking.
Security bag: Bandit, Semgrep, gitleaks, Trivy/Grype container scans, SBOM and signing on PRs, merge-queue candidates, maintained-branch pushes and a daily schedule.
Dead-code ratchet: vulture findings are held to the reviewed per-identity ledger in quality/vulture-baseline.json on every PR and merge-queue candidate.

replaced_by: scripts/check-suite-inventory.py (collected node-ID inventory, stricter than the annotation scan)
.github/workflows/ci.yml and .github/workflows/quality.yml (root test failures are blocking, not advisory)
workflows.rationale: The 'Stream 1 Diagnostic' workflow triggered only on feat/execution-runtime-spine-373 -- a branch deleted after #373 landed -- and pinned a baseline commit that no longer exists, while every step ended in `|| true`. It could never run, and had it run it could never fail: the definition of an always-green precedent (#400). Removed; its three annotations are covered by blocking gates.

On-demand #301 / ADR-082226-5104 §8 working-memory projection benchmark (per-projection RAM, hydration cost, recall and traversal latency at caller-supplied concurrency); deterministic and offline, run when the memory substrate changes — a measurement, not a gate.

On-demand #916 (RESEARCH M8-B3) model-routing benchmark (scripts/bench_model_routing.py: outcome-learned policies vs the shipped static scorer under delayed, sparsified, drifting feedback, plus clipped-IPS/doubly-robust off-policy evaluation); deterministic and offline, re-measured when the router, the world model, or the policies change — a measurement, not a gate.

retained_branches.reason: Retired branch per .github/branch-protection.json ('The live topology is topic branches -> develop -> main.'), yet still named in the push.branches filter of ci/quality/security/formal-conformance/gate-c/registry/vulture-ratchet/compliance-evidence/devskim. Retained so the gate set still applies if the branch is ever re-created; deleting the retired triggers is owned cleanup, and this row is what makes the dead reference visible instead of silent (SPEC-231 records the four-tier model it belonged to).

Transient maintenance branch of the retired integration flow, still named in ci.yml's push.branches (SPEC-231). Same retention rationale as `integration`: the trigger is a reviewed decision, and a push to a re-created branch must still receive the gate set.
